options.label: Machine Type (Restart)
options.info: Manually select the machine type you would like the core to start in.

options.label: Real-Time Clock Source (Restart)
options.info: Initial time of the emulated real-time clock (MSX2 and later). 'Host Clock' matches your computer's clock. 'Fixed Epoch' always starts at 1985-01-01 00:00:00, making emulation bit-identical between runs for netplay, run-ahead and input replay. The clock advances from emulated time either way.

options.label: Crop Overscan
options.info: Forces cropping of overscanned frames

options.label: VDP Sync Type (Restart)
options.info: Match the game/machine region frequency to avoid emulated speed issues.

options.label: No Sprite Limit
options.info: Remove the 4 sprite per line limit which can reduce or remove sprite flicker in some games.

options.label: Sound YM2413 Enable (Restart)
options.info: Awaiting description.

options.label: Additional MSX Sound Cartridge (Restart)
options.info: Additional MSX sound cartridge to insert to the first free slot.

options.label: I/O Sound Enable
options.info: Enable the I/O sound (floppy disk access sound).

options.label: Colecovision Keyboard Mapping
options.info: Additionally, use the keyboard for the Colecovision 0-9, #, and * buttons. Player 1: 0-9, # is -, and * is =; Player 2: Keypad 0-9, # is /, and * is *. Gamepad mappings also work.

options.label: Use F12 to hard reset and restart emulation
options.info: Use key F12 to hard reset and restart emulation like blueMSX standalone

options.label: Cart Mapper Type (Restart)
options.info: When a ROM game or application is in the database, the emulator uses the databases to apply the correct mapper. If the sha1 value of a dump is not yet in the databases, it uses an automatic mapper detection system, but it can fail in some cases. In this situation, you can manually select the correct mapper.

options.label: Patch Colecovision ROM Fast Boot (Close Content)
options.info: Patch the NTSC Colecovision ROM for fast booting (3.3s)

options.label: Tape Loading Speed
options.info: Fast-forward while the tape is running and the program frequently reads its input. Internal timing is unchanged. Toggle frontend fast-forward off to cancel until the tape stops. Requires frontend fast-forward override support.

options.label: Region
options.info: Force core to use NTSC, PAL or Dendy region timings.

options.label: Game Genie Add-On (Restart Required)
options.info: Enable emulation of a Game Genie add-on cartridge, allowing cheat codes to be entered when launching games. The Game Genie ROM file 'gamegenie.nes' must be present in the frontend's system directory. Does not apply to FDS or arcade content.

options.label: Show Advanced System Options
options.info: Show advanced system options and tweaks.

options.label: Show Advanced Sound Options
options.info: Show advanced sound options and tweaks.

options.label: Aspect Ratio
options.info: Choose preferred aspect ratio.

options.label: Color Palette
options.info: Choose from pre-generated palettes, a custom 64x3 palette from file or raw format (needs to use a nes-decoder shader).

options.label: NTSC Filter
options.info: Blargg's NTSC filters are used to replicate RF, Composite, S-Video, and RGB cable signals.

options.label: Sound Quality
options.info: Enable higher quality sound. Increases performance requirements.

options.label: Audio RF Filter
options.info: Apply a low pass audio filter to simulate the 'muted' sound of the NES when connected to a television via the RF modulator.

options.label: Stereo Sound Effect
options.info: Enable a fake stereo sound effect by delaying the right audio channel when upmixing the mono signal output from the NES.

options.label: Swap Audio Duty Cycles
options.info: Simulates the sound from famiclones that have the pulse wave channels duty cycle bits reversed.

options.label: Master Volume
options.info: Change master volume level.

options.label: Audio Channel 1 (Square 1)
options.info: Enables or disables pulse wave generator audio output 1.

options.label: Audio Channel 2 (Square 2)
options.info: Enables or disables pulse wave generator audio output 2.

options.label: Audio Channel 3 (Triangle)
options.info: Enables or disables triangle wave generator audio output.

options.label: Audio Channel 4 (Noise)
options.info: Enables or disables noise generator audio output.

options.label: Audio Channel 5 (PCM)
options.info: Enables or disables delta modulation channel audio output.

options.label: Turbo Enable
options.info: Enables or disables turbo buttons.

options.label: Turbo Delay (in frames)

options.label: Zapper Mode
options.info: Selects device to use for Zapper games.

options.label: Show Zapper Crosshair
options.info: Shows or hides on-screen crosshairs when using a Zapper.

options.label: Zapper Tolerance
options.info: Sets how many pixels from target area is on target.

options.label: Invert Zapper Trigger Signal
options.info: Inverts trigger logic when using a Zapper. Disabling it resembles original hardware behavior.

options.label: Invert Zapper Sensor Signal
options.info: Inverts sensor logic when using a Zapper (Sequential Targets Light gun mode only). Disabling it resembles original NES/FC hardware behavior.

options.label: Arkanoid Mode
options.info: Selects device to use for Arkanoid games.

options.label: Mouse Sensitivity
options.info: Mouse sensitivity in percent.

options.label: Allow Opposing Directions
options.info: Allows simultaneous UP+DOWN or LEFT+RIGHT button combinations, which can create different effects in some games.

options.label: No Sprite Limit
options.info: Removes the 8-per-scanline hardware limit. This reduces sprite flickering but can cause some games to glitch since some use this for effects.

options.label: Overclock
options.info: Enables or disables overclocking, which can reduce slowdowns in some games. Postrender method is more compatible with every game, Vblank is more effective for games like Contra Force.

options.label: RAM Power-On Fill (Restart Required)
options.info: RAM values on power up. Some games rely on initial RAM values for random number generation as an example.

options.label: Auto-select Model for 128K content (needs content load)
options.info: Load 128K-only releases on a Spectrum 128K even when Model is set to a 48K machine. A tape is treated as 128K-only when it says so itself (a 'stop the tape if in 48K mode' block, or hardware information ruling out a 48K) or when its filename tags it as the 128K release. Leave this disabled to have Model always honoured exactly as set; the core still says so on screen when content looks like it needs a 128K.

options.label: Issue 2 Keyboard
options.info: Emulate an Issue 2 Spectrum, which returns a different value for the unused bits of the keyboard port. A handful of 48K titles (Rasputin and others) only respond to the keyboard on an Issue 2 machine. No effect on 128K and later models.

options.label: Fuller Box
options.info: Emulate the Fuller Box AY-3-8912 audio interface (ports 0x3f/0x5f) and its joystick port. Leave disabled for plain 48K titles: some of them poke those ports and will play AY music that no unexpanded Spectrum could produce. Selecting the Fuller joystick on a controller port enables the box regardless of this setting. Changing this resets the machine.

options.label: Currah uSpeech
options.info: Emulate the Currah uSpeech allophone speech synthesiser. Requires two ROM images the core cannot distribute, 'uspeech.rom' and 'sp0256-al2.bin', placed in the frontend's system directory; without them the option has no effect. Changing this resets the machine.

options.label: Melodik
options.info: Emulate the Melodik AY-3-8912 audio interface, which decodes the 128K AY ports (0xfffd/0xbffd) on a 48K machine. Changing this resets the machine.

options.label: AY Volume
options.info: Relative volume of the AY-3-8912 chip, so AY music can be turned down without losing beeper effects (or the other way round).

options.label: Beeper Volume
options.info: Relative volume of the ULA beeper.

options.label: Time to Release Key in ms
Use Auto Size for Savestates. For Netplay 'Off' is recommended
GB Colorization
options.info: Enables colorization of Game Boy games. 'Auto' selects the 'best' (most colorful/appropriate) palette. 'GBC' selects game-specific Game Boy Color palette if defined, otherwise 'GBC - Dark Green'. 'SGB' selects game-specific Super Game Boy palette if defined, otherwise 'SGB - 1A'. 'Internal' uses 'Internal Palette' core option. 'Custom' loads user-created palette from system directory.

options.label: Internal Palette
options.info: Selects palette used for colorizing Game Boy games when 'GB Colorization' is set to 'Internal', or when 'GB Colorization' is set to 'Auto' and game has no pre-defined SGB/GBC palette. 'GB' palettes mimic the display of original Game Boy hardware. 'GBC' palettes are identical to the built-in presets of the Game Boy Color. 'SGB' palettes are identical to the built-in presets of the Super Game Boy.

options.label: > TWB64 - Pack 1 Palette
options.info: Selects internal colorization palette when 'Internal Palette' is set to 'TWB64 - Pack 1'.

options.label: > TWB64 - Pack 2 Palette
options.info: Selects internal colorization palette when 'Internal Palette' is set to 'TWB64 - Pack 2'.

options.label: > TWB64 - Pack 3 Palette
options.info: Selects internal colorization palette when 'Internal Palette' is set to 'TWB64 - Pack 3'.

options.label: > PixelShift - Pack 1 Palette
options.info: Selects internal colorization palette when 'Internal Palette' is set to 'PixelShift - Pack 1'.

options.label: Color Correction
options.info: Adjusts output colors to match the display of real Game Boy Color hardware. 'GBC Only' ensures that correction will only be applied when playing Game Boy Color games, or when using a Game Boy Color palette to colorize a Game Boy game. 'Always' applies color correction to all content, and will produce unexpected/suboptimal results when using 'GB' or 'SGB' internal color palettes.

options.label: Color Correction Mode
options.info: Specifies method used when performing color correction. 'Accurate' produces output almost indistinguishable from a real Game Boy Color LCD panel. 'Fast' merely darkens colors and reduces saturation, and may be used on low-end hardware if the 'Accurate' method is too slow.

options.label: Color Correction - Frontlight Position
options.info: Simulates the physical response of the Game Boy Color LCD panel when illuminated from different angles. 'Central' represents standard color reproduction. 'Above Screen' increases brightness. 'Below Screen' reduces brightness. This setting only applies when 'Color Correction Mode' is set to 'Accurate'.

options.label: Dark Filter Level (%)
options.info: Enable luminosity-based brightness reduction. May be used to avoid glare/eye strain when playing games with white backgrounds, which are intended for display on a non-backlit Game Boy Color and can therefore appear uncomfortably bright when viewed on a modern backlit screen.

options.label: Interframe Blending
options.info: Simulates LCD ghosting effects. 'Simple' performs a 50:50 mix of the current and previous frames. 'LCD Ghosting' mimics natural LCD response times by combining multiple buffered frames. 'Simple' blending is required when playing games that rely on LCD ghosting for transparency effects (Wave Race, Ballistic, Chikyuu Kaihou Gun ZAS...).

options.label: Audio Resampler
options.info: Specify which algorithm to use when resampling generated audio (the Game Boy audio rate is limited only by its CPU write speed, such that 'native' frequencies are impractical on modern sound devices and must be downsampled). 'Sinc' produces the highest quality. 'Cosine' improves performance on low-end hardware.

options.label: Emulated Hardware (Restart Required)
options.info: Specify which type of hardware to emulate. 'Auto' is recommended. Selecting 'GBA' unlocks extra features in certain 'GBA Enhanced' Game Boy Color games (Shantae, Wendy - Every Witch Way, Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons/Ages...).

options.label: Use Official Bootloader (Restart Required)
options.info: Enable support for official Game Boy and Game Boy Color bootloaders, with corresponding start-up logo animations.

options.label: Allow Opposing Directions
options.info: Enabling this will allow pressing/quickly alternating/holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement-based glitches.

options.label: Turbo Button Period
options.info: Specify the repeat interval (in frames) when holding down the Turbo A/B buttons.

options.label: Controller Rumble Strength
options.info: Enables haptic feedback effects for supported games (Pokemon Pinball, Perfect Dark...).

options.label: Show Game Link Settings
options.info: Enable configuration of networked Game Link (multiplayer) options. NOTE: Quick Menu may need to be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.label: Cartridge Hardware (restart)
options.info: Select hardware for cartridge ROMs only. Disks, data packs, playlists and no-content startup always use ADAM.

options.label: ADAM Disk Control Drive
options.info: Choose which drive the frontend Disk Control menu operates. Other drives remain mounted. Loaded media selects the primary content drive.

options.label: ADAM Computer Reset
options.info: Select Reset to boot the computer from mounted media, or SmartWriter when none is bootable. To request it again, select Idle then Reset. Normal frontend Reset retains the current boot mode.

options.label: ADAM Writable Media (restart)
options.info: Disabled mounts ADAM media write protected. Save-directory working copy stores writes in complete images under the frontend save directory and never overwrites source content.

options.label: Refresh Rate (restart)
options.info: Select which refresh rate will be used in emulation. 'Auto' automatically selects the best refresh rate based on the loaded content. 'NTSC (60 Hz)' forces 60 Hz. 'PAL (50 Hz)' forces 50 Hz.

options.label: Mapper (restart)
options.info: Select which mapper (memory bank controller) is emulated. 'Auto' automatically detects the appropriate mapper based on the loaded content. Only change this if a game does not work correctly with the default setting.

options.label: Video Chip (restart)
options.info: Select the installed video chip. 'Auto' uses TMS9918A unless the loaded game database entry requires F18A. Changes take effect when content is restarted.

options.label: Aspect Ratio
options.info: Select which aspect ratio will be presented by the core. '1:1 PAR' selects an aspect ratio that produces square pixels.

options.label: Overscan
options.info: Select which overscan (borders) will be used in TMS9918A emulation. 'Disabled' shows no overscan. 'Top+Bottom' enables vertical overscan only. 'Full (284 width)' and 'Full (320 width)' enable full overscan with different horizontal widths. F18A output uses its active logical raster without TMS overscan.

options.label: No Sprite Limit
options.info: Remove the per-line sprite limit. This reduces flickering but may cause glitches in certain games. It's best to keep this option disabled.

options.label: Allow Up+Down / Left+Right
options.info: Allow pressing, quickly alternating, or holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement based glitches in certain games.

options.label: Spinner Support
options.info: Select which spinner controller will be emulated. Spinners are controlled by mouse movement. Mouse buttons are mapped to Left (Yellow) and Right (Red) buttons.

options.label: Spinner Sensitivity
options.info: Set the sensitivity of the spinner controller. 1 is the lowest sensitivity and 10 is the highest.

options.label: System Hardware
options.info: Runs loaded content with a specific emulated console. 'Auto' will select the most appropriate system for the current game.

options.label: System Region
options.info: Specify which region the system is from. For consoles other than the Game Gear, 'PAL' is 50 Hz, while 'NTSC' is 60 Hz. Games may run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

options.label: Force VDP Mode
options.info: Overrides the VDP mode to force it to run at either NTSC 60Hz or PAL 50Hz, regardless of system region.

options.label: System Boot ROM
options.info: Use official BIOS/bootloader for emulated hardware, if present in RetroArch's system directory. Displays console-specific start-up sequence/animation, then runs loaded content.

options.label: CD System BRAM (Requires Restart)
options.info: When running Sega CD/Mega-CD content, specifies whether to share a single save file between all games from a specific region (Per-BIOS) or to create a separate save file for each game (Per-Game). Note that the Sega CD/Mega-CD has limited internal storage, sufficient only for a handful of titles. To avoid running out of space, the 'Per-Game' setting is recommended.

options.label: CD Backup Cart BRAM (Requires Restart)
options.info: When running Sega CD/Mega-CD content, specifies whether to share a single backup ram cart for all games (Per-Cart) or to create a separate backup ram cart for each game (Per-Game).

options.label: CD Backup Cart BRAM Size (Requires Restart)
options.info: Sets the backup ram cart size when running Sega CD/Mega-CD content. Useful when setting the backup ram cart to Per-Game to avoid multiple larger cart sizes.

options.label: CD add-on (MD mode) (Requires Restart)
options.info: Specify which add-on to use for CD audio playback with supported Mega Drive/Genesis games.

options.label: Cartridge Lock-On
options.info: Lock-On Technology is a Mega Drive/Genesis feature that allowed an older game to connect to the pass-through port of a special cartridge for extended or altered gameplay. This option specifies which type of special 'lock-on' cartridge to emulate. A corresponding bios file must be present in RetroArch's system directory.

options.label: Core-Provided Aspect Ratio
options.info: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

options.label: Borders
options.info: Enable this to display the overscan regions at the top/bottom and/or left/right of the screen. These would normally be hidden by the bezel around the edge of a standard-definition television.

options.label: Hide Master System Side Borders
options.info: Cuts off 8 pixels from either the left side of the screen, or both left and right sides when running Master System games.

options.label: Game Gear Extended Screen
options.info: Forces Game Gear titles to run in SMS mode, with an increased resolution of 256x192. May show additional content, but typically displays a border of corrupt/unwanted image data.

options.label: Blargg NTSC Filter
options.info: Apply a video filter to mimic various NTSC TV signals.

options.label: LCD Ghosting Filter
options.info: Apply an image 'ghosting' filter to mimic the display characteristics of the Game Gear and Genesis Nomad LCD panels.

options.label: Interlaced Mode 2 Output
options.info: Interlaced Mode 2 allows the Mega Drive/Genesis to output a double height (high resolution) 320x448 image by drawing alternate scan lines each frame (this is used by Sonic the Hedgehog 2 and Combat Cars multiplayer modes). 'Double Field' mimics original hardware, producing a sharp image with flickering/interlacing artifacts. 'Single Field' applies a deinterlacing filter, which stabilizes the image but causes mild blurring.

options.label: Frameskip
options.info: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilizes the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.info: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: Master System FM (YM2413)
options.info: Enable emulation of the FM Sound Unit used by certain Sega Mark III/Master System games for enhanced audio output.

options.label: Master System FM (YM2413) Core
options.info: Select method used to emulate the FM Sound Unit of the Sega Mark III/Master System. 'MAME' option is fast, and runs full speed on most systems. 'Nuked' option is cycle accurate, very high quality, and has substantial CPU requirements.

options.label: Mega Drive/Genesis FM
options.info: Select method used to emulate the FM synthesizer (main sound generator) of the Mega Drive/Genesis. 'MAME' options are fast, and run full speed on most systems. 'Nuked' options are cycle accurate, very high quality, and have substantial CPU requirements. The YM2612 chip is used by the original Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis. The YM3438 is used in later Mega Drive/Genesis revisions.

options.label: Sound Output
options.info: Select stereo or mono sound playback.

options.label: Audio Filter
options.info: Enable a low pass audio filter to better simulate the characteristic sound of a Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis.

options.label: Low-Pass Filter %
options.info: Specify the cut-off frequency of the audio low pass filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: PSG Preamp Level
options.info: Set the audio preamplifier level of the emulated SN76496 4-channel Programmable Sound Generator found in the SG-1000, Sega Mark III, Master System, Game Gear and Mega Drive/Genesis.

options.label: FM Preamp Level
options.info: Set the audio preamplifier level of the emulated Mega Drive/Genesis FM sound synthesizer or Sega Mark III/Master System FM Sound Unit.

options.label: CD-DA Volume
options.info: Adjust the mixing volume of the emulated CD audio playback output.

options.label: PCM Volume
options.info: Adjust the mixing volume of the emulated Sega CD/Mega-CD RF5C164 PCM sound generator output.

options.label: EQ Low
options.info: Adjust the low range band of the internal audio equalizer.

options.label: EQ Mid
options.info: Adjust the middle range band of the internal audio equalizer.

options.label: EQ High
options.info: Adjust the high range band of the internal audio equalizer.

options.label: Light Gun Input
options.info: Use a mouse-controlled 'Light Gun' or 'Touchscreen' input.

options.label: Show Light Gun Crosshair
options.info: Display light gun crosshairs when using the MD Menacer, MD Justifiers and MS Light Phaser input device types.

options.label: Invert Mouse Y-Axis
options.info: Inverts the Y-axis of the MD Mouse input device type.

options.label: Remove Per-Line Sprite Limit
options.info: Removes the original sprite-per-scanline hardware limit. This reduces flickering but can cause visual glitches, as some games exploit the hardware limit to generate special effects.

options.label: Enhanced per-tile vertical scroll
options.info: Allows each individual cell to be scrolled vertically, instead of 16px 2-cell, by averaging out with the vscroll value of the neighbouring cell. This hack only applies to few games that use 2-cell vertical scroll mode.

options.label: Enhanced per-tile vertical scroll limit
options.info: Only when Enhanced per-tile vertical scroll is enabled. Adjusts the limit of the vertical scroll enhancement. When the vscroll difference between neighbouring tiles is bigger than this limit, the enhancement is disabled.

options.label: CPU Speed
options.info: Overclock the emulated CPU. Can reduce slowdown, but may cause glitches.

options.label: System Lock-Ups
options.info: Emulate system lock-ups that occur on real hardware when performing illegal address access. This should only be disabled when playing certain demos and homebrew that rely on illegal behavior for correct operation.

options.label: 68K Address Error
options.info: The Mega Drive/Genesis main CPU (Motorola 68000) generates an Address Error exception (crash) when attempting to perform unaligned memory access. Enabling this will simulate this behavior. It should only be disabled when playing ROM hacks, since these are typically developed using less accurate emulators and may rely on invalid RAM access for correct operation.

options.label: CD Access Time
options.info: Simulate original CD hardware latency when initiating a read or seeking to a specific location on loaded disc. This is required by a few CD games that crash if CD data is available too soon and also fixes CD audio desync issues in some games. Disabling this can be useful with MSU-MD games as it makes CD audio tracks loops more seamless.

options.label: CD Image Cache
options.info: Load CD image to memory on startup. CHD supported only. Restart Required.

options.label: Show Advanced Audio Volume Settings (Reopen menu)
options.info: Enable configuration of low-level audio channel parameters. NOTE: Quick Menu must be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.info: Set video update frequency. Internally, the Lynx renders at a variable rate from 0 to 75Hz. Frames that occur between video update events will be dropped. Higher rates may increase video smoothness (depending on actual game frame rate) but can cause tearing on 60Hz displays.

options.info: Rotate the virtual console screen to achieve the correct layout of 'portrait' oriented games on a conventional (landscape) display.

options.label: LCD Ghosting Filter
options.info: Apply an image 'ghosting' effect by blending multiple successive video frames. options.info: When RUN and SELECT are pressed simultaneously, disable both buttons temporarily instead of resetting.

options.label: P1 Default Joypad Type
options.info: Choose if port 1 joypad should be 2 or 6 buttons by default. This option is only applied when the core starts, if you want to switch while content is running, use the 'Mode Switch' button. NOTE: 6 buttons joypad can have weird behaviors in non compatible games.

options.label: P2 Default Joypad Type
options.info: Choose if port 2 joypad should be 2 or 6 buttons by default. This option is only applied when the core starts, if you want to switch while content is running, use the 'Mode Switch' button. NOTE: 6 buttons joypad can have weird behaviors in non compatible games.

options.label: P3 Default Joypad Type
options.info: Choose if port 3 joypad should be 2 or 6 buttons by default. This option is only applied when the core starts, if you want to switch while content is running, use the 'Mode Switch' button. NOTE: 6 buttons joypad can have weird behaviors in non compatible games.

options.label: P4 Default Joypad Type
options.info: Choose if port 4 joypad should be 2 or 6 buttons by default. This option is only applied when the core starts, if you want to switch while content is running, use the 'Mode Switch' button. NOTE: 6 buttons joypad can have weird behaviors in non compatible games.

options.label: P5 Default Joypad Type
options.info: Choose if port 5 joypad should be 2 or 6 buttons by default. This option is only applied when the core starts, if you want to switch while content is running, use the 'Mode Switch' button. NOTE: 6 buttons joypad can have weird behaviors in non compatible games.

options.label: Turbo Toggle
options.info: Enable the turbo toggle hotkeys (buttons III and IV).

options.label: Alternate Turbo Hotkey
options.info: Assign RetroPad's L3/R3 buttons as turbo toggle hotkeys instead of buttons III and IV. Works only as long as nothing is assigned to the L3/R3 buttons. You can avoid remapping buttons III and IV when switching to 6-button controller mode with this.

options.label: Turbo Delay
options.info: Adjust the time between turbo fire (in frames).

options.label: CD Image Cache (Restart Required)
options.info: Load the complete image into memory at startup. Can potentially decrease loading times at the cost of an increased startup time.

options.label: CD BIOS (Restart Required)
options.info: Most games can run on 'System Card 3'. 'Games Express' is needed for several unlicensed games.

options.label: (CD) CD Speed
options.info: Higher values enable faster loading times but can cause issues with a couple of games.

options.label: (CD) ADPCM Volume %
options.info: CD game only. Setting this volume control too high may cause sample clipping.

options.label: (CD) CDDA Volume %
options.info: CD game only. Setting this volume control too high may cause sample clipping.

options.label: (CD) PSG Volume %
options.info: CD game only. Setting this volume control too high may cause sample clipping.

options.label: No Sprite Limit
options.info: Remove 16-sprites-per-scanline hardware limit. WARNING: May cause graphics glitching on some games.

options.label: CPU Overclock Multiplier (Restart Required)
options.info: Higher values can reduce slowdowns in games. WARNING: Can cause glitches and crashes.

options.label: 3D mode (requires restart)
options.info: Select the 3D mode. Anaglyph - used in conjunction with classic dual-lens-color glasses. Cyberscope - intended for use with the CyberScope 3D device. sidebyside - the left-eye image is displayed on the left, and the right-eye image is displayed on the right. vli - Vertical lines alternate between left and right view. hli - Horizontal lines alternate between left and right view. Does not apply to VR mode.

options.label: Anaglyph preset
options.info: Anaglyph preset colors.

options.label: Side-by-side separation
options.info: Number of pixels to separate left and right views in side-by-side 3D mode.

options.label: Allow Opposite Directions
options.info: Allow pressing up and down or left and right directions at the same time. This may cause glitches.

options.label: CPU emulation  (Restart)
options.info: Choose between faster and accurate (slower) emulation.

options.label: VR
options.info: Enabled shows both eyes as a stereo screen whenever the frontend presents them, in a headset or a stereo display mode. Disabled keeps the chosen 3D mode. Head-locked holds the screen in front of the eyes in a headset (requires restart).

options.label: Display Rotation
options.info: Choose the orientation of the console screen. 'Portrait' can be used to achieve the correct layout of portrait oriented games on a conventional (landscape) display. 'Manual' enables rotation via the controller (default button: SELECT).

options.label: Rotate Button Mappings
options.info: Choose the preferred button mapping. 'Auto' adjusts button mapping to match the current display rotation.

options.label: Color Palette
options.info: Choose the colorization of WonderSwan (Mono) games. 'WS' palettes mimic the display of the original WonderSwan hardware.

options.label: Color Depth (Restart Required)
options.info: 24-bit is slower and not available on all platforms.

options.label: Frameskip
options.info: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilizes the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.info: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', this specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: 60Hz Mode
options.info: Update the display at 60Hz instead of the native 75Hz WonderSwan refresh rate by dropping every fifth frame. Reduces video smoothness, but avoids screen tearing on displays that do not support native operation above 60Hz.

options.label: Sound Output Sample Rate
options.info: Higher values improve sound quality slightly at the expense of performance.

options.label: Audio Filter
options.info: Apply a low pass audio filter to 'soften' the sometimes harsh chiptunes produced by the WonderSwan.

options.label: Boot Game Directly
options.info: Choose if the core should boot the game directly or if it should boot to the DS menu instead (BIOS and firmware files required).

options.label: Use Firmware Settings
options.info: Use language and username from the DS firmware. When disabled or if firmware file was not found, the username will be provided by the Libretro frontend, if it's empty it will default to 'melonDS'.

options.label: Language
options.info: Selected language will be used if 'Use Firmware Settings' is disabled or if firmware file was not found.

options.label: Microphone Input
options.info: Choose the type of noise that will be used as microphone input.

options.label: Touch Mode
options.info: Choose mode for interactions with the touch screen.

options.label: Swap Screen Mode
options.info: Choose if the 'Swap screens' button should work on press or on hold.

options.label: Screen Layout
options.info: Choose how many screens should be displayed and how they should be displayed.

options.label: Screen Gap
options.info: Choose how large the gap between the 2 screens should be.

options.label: Hybrid Small Screen Mode
options.info: Choose the position of the small screen when using a 'hybrid' mode, or if it should show both screens.

options.label: Game Boy Model (Restart)
options.info: Runs loaded content with a specific Game Boy model. 'Autodetect' will select the most appropriate model for the current game.

options.label: Use BIOS File if Found (Restart)
options.info: Use official BIOS/bootloader for emulated hardware, if present in RetroArch's system directory.

options.label: Skip BIOS Intro (Restart)
options.info: When using an official BIOS/bootloader, skip the start-up logo animation. This setting is ignored when 'Use BIOS File if Found' is disabled.

options.label: Default Game Boy Palette
options.info: Selects which palette is used for Game Boy games that are not Game Boy Color or Super Game Boy compatible, or if the model is forced to Game Boy.

options.label: Hardware Preset Game Boy Palettes (Restart)
options.info: Use the palettes for Game Boy games that have presets on the Game Boy Color or Super Game Boy.

options.label: Use Super Game Boy Borders (Restart)
options.info: Display Super Game Boy borders when running Super Game Boy enhanced games.

options.label: Color Correction
options.info: Adjusts output colors to match the display of real GBA/GBC hardware.

options.label: Interframe Blending
options.info: Simulates LCD ghosting effects. 'Simple' performs a 50:50 mix of the current and previous frames. 'Smart' attempts to detect screen flickering, and only performs a 50:50 mix on affected pixels. 'LCD Ghosting' mimics natural LCD response times by combining multiple buffered frames. 'Simple' or 'Smart' blending is required when playing games that aggressively exploit LCD ghosting for transparency effects (Wave Race, Chikyuu Kaihou Gun ZAS, F-Zero, the Boktai series...).

options.label: Audio Filter
options.info: Enables a low pass audio filter to reduce the 'harshness' of generated audio.

options.label: Audio Filter Level
options.info: Specifies the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: Allow Opposing Directional Input
options.info: Enabling this will allow pressing / quickly alternating / holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement-based glitches.

options.label: Solar Sensor Level
options.info: Sets ambient sunlight intensity. Can be used by games that included a solar sensor in their cartridges, e.g: the Boktai series.

options.label: Game Boy Player Rumble (Restart)
options.info: Enabling this will allow compatible games with the Game Boy Player boot logo to make the controller rumble. Due to how Nintendo decided this feature should work, it may cause glitches such as flickering or lag in some of these games.

options.label: Idle Loop Removal
options.info: Reduce system load by optimizing so-called 'idle-loops' - sections in the code where nothing happens, but the CPU runs at full speed (like a car revving in neutral). Improves performance, and should be enabled on low-end hardware.

options.label: Frameskip
options.info: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Auto (Threshold)' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting. 'Fixed Interval' utilises the 'Frameskip Interval' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.info: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Auto (Threshold)', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: Frameskip Interval
options.info: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Fixed Interval', the value set here is the number of frames omitted after a frame is rendered - i.e. '0' = 60fps, '1' = 30fps, '2' = 15fps, etc.

options.label: RDP Plugin
options.info: Select a RDP Plugin, use Angrylion (if available) for best compability, GLideN64 for Performance

options.label: 4:3 Resolution
options.info: (GLN64) Select Render Viewport dimensions (4:3).

options.label: Wide Resolution
options.info: (GLN64) Select Render Viewport dimensions for wider resolutions.

options.label: Aspect Ratio
options.info: (GLN64) Select the aspect ratio. 'adjusted' means essentially Widescreen hacks.

options.label: Native Resolution Factor
options.info: (GLN64) Render at N times the native resolution.

options.label: Threaded Renderer
options.info: (GLN64) Use the Threaded Renderer, improves performance but increases input lag.

options.label: Bilinear filtering mode
options.info: (GLN64) Select a Bilinear filtering method, 3point is the original system specific way.

options.label: Hybrid Filter
options.info: (GLN64) Hybrid integer scaling filter, this can be slow with low-end GPUs.

options.label: Dithering
options.info: (GLN64) Applies dithering pattern to output image.

options.label: Dithering Quantization
options.info: (GLN64) Dither with color quantization.

options.label: Image Dithering Mode
options.info: (GLN64) Dithering mode for image in RDRAM.

options.label: MSAA level
options.info: (GLN64) Anti-Aliasing level (0 = disabled).

options.label: FXAA
options.info: (GLN64) Fast Approximate Anti-Aliasing shader, moderately blur textures (0 = disabled).

options.label: LOD Emulation
options.info: (GLN64) Calculate per-pixel Level Of Details to select texture mip levels and blend them with each other using LOD fraction.

options.label: Framebuffer Emulation
options.info: (GLN64) Frame/depth buffer emulation. Disabling it can shorten input lag for particular games, but also break some special effects.

options.label: Copy auxiliary buffers to RDRAM
options.info: (GLN64) Copy auxiliary buffers to RDRAM (fixes some Game artifacts like Paper Mario Intro).

options.label: Color buffer to RDRAM
options.info: (GLN64) Color buffer copy to RDRAM (Off will trade compatibility for Performance).

options.label: Enable color buffer copy from RDRAM
options.info: (GLN64) Enable color buffer copy from RDRAM.

options.label: Depth buffer to RDRAM
options.info: (GLN64) Depth buffer copy to RDRAM (Off will trade compatibility for Performance).

options.label: Background Mode
options.info: (GLN64) Render backgrounds mode (HLE only). One piece (fast), Stripped (precise).

options.label: Hardware per-pixel lighting
options.info: (GLN64) Standard per-vertex lighting when disabled. Slightly different rendering.

options.label: Continuous texrect coords
options.info: (GLN64) Make texrect coordinates continuous to avoid black lines between them.

options.label: Enable inaccurate texture coordinates
options.info: (GLN64) Enables inaccurate texture coordinate calculations. This can improve performance and texture pack compatibity at the cost of accuracy.

options.label: Enable native-res boundaries for texture coordinates
options.info: (GLN64) Bound texture rectangle texture coordinates to the values they take in native resolutions. It prevents garbage due to fetching out of texture bounds, but can result in hard edges.

options.label: Native res. 2D texrects
options.info: (GLN64) Render 2D texrects in native resolution to fix misalignment between parts of 2D image (example: Mario Kart driver selection portraits).

options.label: Less accurate blending mode
options.info: (GLN64) Do not use shaders to emulate N64 blending modes. Works faster on slow GPU. Can cause glitches.

options.label: GPU shader depth write
options.info: (GLN64) Enable writing of fragment depth. Some mobile GPUs do not support it, thus it's optional. Leave enabled.

options.label: N64 Depth Compare
options.info: (GLN64) Enable N64 depth compare instead of OpenGL standard one. Experimental, Fast mode will have more glitches.

options.label: Cache GPU Shaders
options.info: (GLN64) Use persistent storage for compiled shaders.

options.label: Cache Textures
options.info: (GLN64) Save texture cache to hard disk.

options.label: Overscan
options.info: (GLN64) Crop black borders from the overscan region around the screen.

options.label: Overscan Offset (Top)
options.info: (GLN64) Overscan Top Offset.

options.label: Overscan Offset (Left)
options.info: (GLN64) Overscan Left Offset.

options.label: Overscan Offset (Right)
options.info: (GLN64) Overscan Right Offset.

options.label: Overscan Offset (Bottom)
options.info: (GLN64) Overscan Bottom Offset.

options.label: Max High-Res VRAM Limit
options.info: (GLN64) Limit High-Res textures size in VRAM (in MB, 0 = no limit).

options.label: Max texture cache size
options.info: (GLN64) Set Max texture cache size (in elements). Reduce it if you experience black textures leading to a crash.

options.label: Texture filter
options.info: (GLN64) Select Texture Filtering mode.

options.label: Texture Enhancement
options.info: (GLN64) Various Texture Filters ('As-Is' will just cache).

options.label: Don't filter background textures
options.info: (GLN64) Ignore filtering for Background Textures.

options.label: Use High-Res textures
options.info: (GLN64) Enable High-Res Texture packs if available.

options.label: Use High-Res Texture Cache Compression
options.info: (GLN64) Compress created texture caches.

options.label: Use High-Res Full Alpha Channel
options.info: (GLN64) This should be enabled unless it's a old RICE Texture pack.

options.label: Use enhanced Texture Storage
options.info: (GLN64) Use in addition to Texture cache, will use lazy loading and trade memory consumption against loading speeds.

options.label: Use alternative method for High-Res Checksums
options.info: (GLN64) Use an alternative method for High-Res paletted textures CRC calculations.

options.label: Use enhanced Hi-Res Storage
options.info: (GLN64) Use in addition to High-Res textures, will use lazy loading and trade memory consumption against loading speeds.

options.label: INI Behaviour
options.info: (GLN64) Specifies INI Settings behaviour. This should really only contain essential options. Changing this can and will break ROM's, if the correct options aren't set manually. Some options may only be set via INI (fbInfoDisabled).

options.label: CPU Core
options.info: Select the R4300 CPU Backend, use Interpreter for best compability

options.label: RSP Plugin
options.info: Select a RSP Plugin, use HLE for best performance, ParaLLEl for best LLE Performance and CXD4 as LLE fallback

options.label: Frame Duplication
options.info: Enable Frame duplication to improve smoothing on low-end. Different from frameskip.

options.label: Framerate
options.info: Fullspeed will enforce Count per Op 1 and FBEmu settings, this will break some games!

options.label: VI Refresh (Overclock)
options.info: Select a VI Refresh clock, Auto does not impact behaviour, other values override CountPerScanline.

options.label: Disable Expansion Pak
options.info: Force disable Expansion Pak (might improve performance for some games while reducing emulation accuracy, will break games that require it).

options.label: Ignore emulated TLB Exceptions
options.info: (HACK) Ignore emulated TLB Exceptions, this might fix some broken romhacks. This option might be removed in the future.

values.label: Ignore TLB Exceptions if not using TLB

options.label: Count Per Op
options.info: Count per Op is used to approximate the Counter reg, 0 will use the embedded Database (or default to 2). Changing this will break stuff!

options.label: Count Per Op Divider (Overclock)
options.info: Denominator for Count per Op (allowing sub-1 Count per Op in practice). Changing this can break stuff!

options.label: Analog Deadzone (percent)
options.info: Size of the non responsive area around an analog stick.

options.label: Analog Sensitivity (percent)
options.info: Adjust how far the stick needs to be moved to reach its max value.

options.label: Right C Button
options.info: Select Right C Button mapping.

options.label: Left C Button
options.info: Select Left C Button mapping.

options.label: Down C Button
options.info: Select Down C Button mapping.

options.label: Up C Button
options.info: Select Up C Button mapping.

options.label: Independent C-button Controls
options.info: Use an alternate control scheme, useful for some 3rdparty controllers.

options.label: Player 1 Pak
options.info: Select Player 1 Controller Pak.

options.label: Player 2 Pak
options.info: Select Player 2 Controller Pak.

options.label: Player 3 Pak
options.info: Select Player 3 Controller Pak.

options.label: Player 4 Pak
options.info: Select Player 4 Controller Pak.

options.label: Emulated Hardware (Restart)
options.info: Specify which console hardware to emulate. Requires the corresponding bios file to be present in the frontend 'system' directory (o2rom.bin, c52.bin, g7400.bin, jopac.bin).

options.label: Console Region (Restart)
options.info: Specify which region the system is from. 'Auto' chooses the correct region based on emulated hardware. 'NTSC' is 60hz, 'PAL' is 50hz. Games may run abnormally if the wrong region is selected, and the setting my be overridden if the current content is incompatible.

options.label: Swap Gamepads
options.info: Swap inputs from the two connected controllers of the emulated console. Required for games such as UFO and P.T. Barnum's Acrobats, which accept player 1 input from the second controller.

options.label: Virtual KBD Transparency
options.info: Set transparency level of the virtual on-screen keyboard.

options.label: Crop Overscan
options.info: Remove the border around the edges of the screen, typically unused by games and hidden by the bezel of a standard-definition television.

options.label: Interframe Blending
options.info: Simulate CRT phosphor ghosting effects. 'Simple' performs a 50:50 mix of the current and previous frames. 'Ghosting' accumulates pixels from multiple successive frames. May be used to alleviate screen flicker.

options.label: Audio Volume
options.info: Set output audio volume level.

options.label: Voice Volume
options.info: Set output volume level of 'The Voice' speech samples. The voice sampleset WAV files must be placed in the frontend 'system/voice' directory.

options.label: Audio Filter
options.info: Apply a low pass audio filter to soften the 'harsh' sound effects produced by most Odyssey2/Videopac+ games.

options.label: Audio Filter Level
options.info: Specify the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: Region
options.info: Specify which region the system is from. 'NTSC' is 60 Hz while 'PAL' is 50 Hz. 'Auto' will detect the region of the currently loaded content. Games may run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

options.label: BIOS Selection
options.info: Specify which BIOS to use. 'Auto' will attempt to load a real bios file from the frontend 'system' directory, falling back to high level emulation if unavailable. 'HLE' forces high level BIOS emulation. It is recommended to use an official bios file for better compatibility.

options.label: Show BIOS Name/Boot Logo
options.info: When using a custom BIOS file, enables the display of its file name in the OSD. Also specifies whether to show the BIOS logo when starting or selecting Reset. Warning: Enabling the logo may reduce game compatibility.

options.label: Memory Card 2 Type
options.info: Same as above, but card in slot 2.

options.label: CD read-ahead
options.info: Reads the specified amount of sectors ahead of time to try to avoid later stalls. Affects both physical CD-ROM and CD images. 333000 will try to read the complete disk (requires an additional 750MB of RAM).

options.label: Dynamic Recompiler
options.info: Dynamically recompile PSX CPU instructions to native instructions. Much faster than using an interpreter, but may be less accurate on some platforms.

options.label: DynaRec threading
options.info: Run the dynarec on another thread.

options.label: PSX CPU Clock Speed (%)
options.info: Overclock or under-clock the PSX CPU. Should be much less than 100 (something like 57) due to some real hardware slowdowns not being emulated. Usually should be left at 'Auto', else glitches or hangs are likely.

options.label: Dithering Pattern
options.info: Enable emulation of the dithering technique used by the PSX to smooth out color banding artifacts. "Force" enables it even if the game turns it off. Increases performance requirements.

options.label: Frameskip
options.info: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Auto (Threshold)' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting. 'Fixed Interval' utilises the 'Frameskip Interval' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.info: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Auto (Threshold)', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: Frameskip Interval
options.info: Specify the maximum number of frames that can be skipped before a new frame is rendered.

options.label: Display Internal FPS
options.info: Show the internal frame rate at which the emulated system is rendering content. Note: Requires on-screen notifications to be enabled in the libretro frontend.

options.label: Use fractional frame rate
options.info: Instead of the exact 50 or 60 (maximum) fps for PAL/NTSC the real console runs closer to something like 49.75 and 59.81fps (varies slightly between hw versions). PCSX-ReARMed uses the former "round" framerates to better match modern displays, however that may cause audio/video desync in games like DDR and Spyro 2 (intro). With this option you can try to use fractional framerates.

options.label: RGB32 output
options.info: Improves color depth for true color modes (most FMVs and occasional title screens). Causes higher CPU usage due to double memory bandwidth requirement, even in 15bpp modes. Takes effect on game reload only (libretro limitation).

options.label: (GPU) Slow linked list processing
options.info: Slower but more accurate GPU linked list processing. Needed by only a few games like Vampire Hunter D. Should be autodetected in most cases.

options.label: (GPU) Horizontal overscan
options.info: The PSX can display graphics way into the horizontal borders, even if most screens would crop it. This option tries to display all such graphics. Note that this may result in unusual resolutions that your device might not handle well. The 'Hack' option is intended for the widescreen hacks.

options.label: (GPU) Screen centering
options.info: The PSX has a feature allowing it to shift the image position on screen. Some (mostly PAL) games used this feature in a strange way making the image miscentered and causing uneven borders to appear. With 'Auto' the emulator tries to correct this miscentering automatically. 'Game-controlled' uses the settings supplied by the game. 'Manual' allows to override those values with the settings below.

options.label: (GPU) Manual position X
options.info: X offset of the frame buffer. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

options.label: (GPU) Manual position Y
options.info: Y offset of the frame buffer. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

options.label: (GPU) Manual height adjustment
options.info: Height adjustment. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

options.label: (GPU) Show Interlaced Video
options.info: When enabled, games that run in high resolution video modes (480i, 512i) will produced interlaced video output. While this displays correctly on CRT televisions, it will produce artifacts on modern displays. When disabled, all video is output in progressive format. Note: there are games that will glitch is this is off.

options.label: (GPU) Enhanced Resolution
options.info: Render games that do not already run in high resolution video modes (480i, 512i) at twice the native internal resolution. Improves the fidelity of 3D models at the expense of increased performance requirements. 2D elements are generally unaffected by this setting.

options.label: (GPU) Enhanced Resolution Speed Hack
options.info: ('Enhanced Resolution' Hack) Improves performance but reduces compatibility and may cause rendering errors.

options.label: (GPU) Enhanced Resolution Texture Adjustment
options.info: ('Enhanced Resolution' Hack) Solves some texturing issues in some games in Enhanced Resolution mode. May cause a small performance hit.

options.label: Show Advanced P.E.Op.S. GPU Settings
options.info: Show low-level configuration options for the P.E.Op.S. GPU plugin. Quick Menu may need to be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.label: Show Advanced UNAI GPU Settings
options.info: Show low-level configuration options for the UNAI GPU plugin. Quick Menu may need to be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.label: Audio Reverb Effects
options.info: Enable emulation of the reverb feature provided by the PSX SPU. Can be disabled to improve performance at the expense of reduced audio quality/authenticity.

options.label: Sound Interpolation
options.info: Enable emulation of the in-built audio interpolation provided by the PSX SPU. 'Gaussian' sounds closest to original hardware. 'Simple' improves performance but reduces quality. 'Cubic' has the highest performance requirements but produces increased clarity. Can be disabled entirely for maximum performance, at the expense of greatly reduced audio quality.

options.label: CD Audio
options.info: Enable playback of CD (CD-DA) audio tracks. Can be disabled to improve performance in games that include CD audio, at the expense of missing music.

options.label: XA Decoding
options.info: Enable playback of XA (eXtended Architecture ADPCM) audio tracks. Can be disabled to improve performance in games that include XA audio, at the expense of missing music.

options.label: Show Input Settings
options.info: Show configuration options for all input devices: analog response, Multitaps, light guns, etc. Quick Menu may need to be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.label: Analog Axis Bounds
options.info: Specify range limits for the left and right analog sticks when input device is set to 'analog' or 'dualshock'. 'Square' bounds improve input response when using controllers with highly circular ranges that are unable to fully saturate the X and Y axes at 45 degree deflections.

options.label: Rumble Effects
options.info: Enable haptic feedback when using a rumble-equipped gamepad with input device set to 'dualshock'.

options.label: DualShock Analog Mode Toggle Key Combo
options.info: When the input device type is DualShock, this option allows the emulated DualShock to be toggled between DIGITAL and ANALOG mode like original hardware. You can select the button combination for this.

options.label: Multitap Mode
options.info: Connect a virtual PSX Multitap peripheral to either controller 'Port 1' or controller 'Port 2' for 5 player simultaneous input, or to both 'Ports 1 and 2' for 8 player input. Mutlitap usage requires compatible games.

options.label: NegCon Twist Deadzone
options.info: Set the deadzone of the RetroPad left analog stick when simulating the 'twist' action of emulated neGcon Controllers. Used to eliminate drift/unwanted input.

options.label: NegCon Twist Response
options.info: Specify the analog response when using a RetroPad left analog stick to simulate the 'twist' action of emulated neGcon Controllers.

options.label: Mouse Sensitivity
options.info: Adjust responsiveness of emulated 'mouse' input devices.

options.label: Player 1 Lightgun Crosshair
options.info: Toggle player 1's crosshair for the Guncon or Konami Gun. Only works if RGB32 output is off (video options).

options.label: Player 2 Lightgun Crosshair
options.info: Toggle player 2's crosshair for the Guncon or Konami Gun. Only works if RGB32 output is off (video options).

options.label: Konami Gun X Axis Offset
options.info: Apply an X axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Konami Gun (Hyper Blaster / Justifier) device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Konami Gun Y Axis Offset
options.info: Apply a Y axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Konami Gun (Hyper Blaster / Justifier) device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Guncon X Axis Offset
options.info: Apply an X axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Guncon Y Axis Offset
options.info: Apply a Y axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Guncon X Axis Response
options.info: Adjust relative magnitude of horizontal light gun motion when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Guncon Y Axis Response
options.info: Adjust relative magnitude of vertical light gun motion when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Instruction Cache Emulation
options.info: Enable emulation of the PSX CPU instruction cache. Improves accuracy at the expense of increased performance overheads. Required for Formula One 2001, Formula One Arcade and Formula One 99. [Interpreter only; partial on lightrec and ARM dynarecs]

options.label: Exception and Breakpoint Emulation
options.info: Enable emulation of some almost never used PSX's debug features. This causes a performance hit, is not useful for games and is intended for PSX homebrew and romhack developers only. Only enable if you know what you are doing. [Interpreter only]

options.label: Turbo CD
options.info: This makes the emulated CD-ROM extremely fast and can reduce loading times in some cases. Warning: many games were not programmed to handle such a speed. The game (or even the emulator) MAY CRASH at ANY TIME if this is enabled.

options.label: Disable Automatic Compatibility Hacks
options.info: By default, PCSX-ReARMed will apply auxiliary compatibility hacks automatically, based on the currently loaded content. This behaviour is required for correct operation, but may be disabled if desired.

options.label: (Speed Hack) Disable SMC Checks
options.info: Will cause crashes when loading, and lead to memory card failure.

options.label: (Speed Hack) Assume GTE Registers Unneeded
options.info: May cause rendering errors.

options.label: (Speed Hack) Disable GTE Flags
options.info: Will cause rendering errors.

options.label: Disable CPU/GTE Stalls
options.info: Will cause some games to run too quickly. Should be disabled in almost all cases. Interpreter only.

options.label: System Region
options.info: Specify which region the system is from. 'PAL'/'Europe' is 50hz while 'NTSC'/'US' is 60hz. Games may run faster or slower than normal (or produce errors) if the incorrect region is selected.

options.label: Master System Type
options.info: Choose which type of hardware (SMS or Game Gear) the core should emulate when running Master System content.

options.label: Master System ROM Mapping
options.info: Choose which ROM mapper the core should apply. 'Auto' will work for a wide range of content, but in some cases automatic detection fails.

options.label: Master System Palette in TMS modes
options.info: Choose which colour palette should be used when an SMS game runs in one of the SG-1000 graphics modes.

options.label: Sega CD RAM Cart
options.info: Emulate a Sega CD RAM cart, used for save game data. WARNING: When enabled, internal save data (BRAM) will be discarded.

options.label: Core-Provided Aspect Ratio
options.info: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core Provided' in the Video settings.

options.label: LCD Ghosting Filter
options.info: Apply an image 'ghosting' filter to mimic the display characteristics of the Game Gear and 'Genesis Nomad' LCD panels.

options.label: Video Renderer
options.info: Specify video rendering method. 'Accurate' is slowest, but most exact. 'Good' is faster, but fails if colors change mid-frame too often. 'Fast' renders the complete frame in one pass, and is incompatible with games that rely on mid-frame palette/sprite table updates.

options.label: Audio Sample Rate (Hz)
options.info: Higher values increase sound quality. Lower values may increase performance. Native is the Mega Drive sound chip rate (~53000). Select this if you want the most accurate audio.

options.label: FM filtering
options.info: Enable filtering for Mega Drive FM sound at non-native bitrates. Sound output will improve, at the price of being noticeably slower

options.label: Master System FM Sound Unit
options.info: Enable emulation of the SMS FM Sound Unit. This produces higher quality audio in some games, but non-Japanese titles may fail to run.

options.label: Mega Drive FM chip type
options.info: Select the Mega Drive/Genesis FM chip type. Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis mostly used YM2612, which produced a distinct distortion. YM3438 was used in model 2 consoles.

options.label: Audio Filter
options.info: Enable a low pass audio filter to better simulate the characteristic sound of a Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis. Note that only Model 1 and its add-ons (Sega CD, 32X) employed a physical low pass filter.

options.label: Low-Pass Filter %
options.info: Specify the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: Input Device 1
options.info: Choose which type of controller is plugged into slot 1. Note that a multiplayer adaptor uses both slots.

options.label: Input Device 2
options.info: Choose which type of controller is plugged into slot 2. This setting is ignored when a multiplayer adaptor is plugged into slot 1.

options.label: Frameskip
options.info: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.info: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: No Sprite Limit
options.info: Removes the original sprite-per-scanline hardware limit. This reduces flickering but can cause visual glitches, as some games exploit the hardware limit to generate special effects.

options.label: 68K Overclock
options.info: Overclock the emulated 68K chip. Can reduce slowdown, but may cause glitches.

options.label: Video Scale (Restart)
options.info: Set internal video scale factor. Increasing the scale factor improves the appearance of the internal 'Dot Matrix' LCD filter.

options.label: 60Hz Mode
options.info: Update the display at 60Hz instead of the native 72Hz Pokemon Mini's refresh rate by dropping every sixth frame. Reduces video smoothness, but avoids screen tearing on displays that do not support native operation above 60Hz.

options.label: LCD Filter
options.info: Select internal screen filter. 'Dot Matrix' produces an LCD effect that mimics real hardware. LCD filters are disabled when 'Video Scale' is set to '1x'.

options.label: LCD Mode
options.info: Specify the greyscale 'color' reproduction characteristics of the emulated liquid crystal display. 'Analog' mimics real hardware. '2 Shades' removes ghosting, but causes flickering in most games.

options.label: LCD Contrast
options.info: Set contrast level of emulated liquid crystal display.

options.label: LCD Brightness
options.info: Set brightness offset of emulated liquid crystal display.

options.label: Palette
options.info: Specify palette used to 'colorize' the emulated liquid crystal display. 'Default' mimics real hardware.

options.label: Piezo Filter
options.info: Use an audio filter to simulate the characteristics of the Pokemon Mini's piezoelectric speaker.

options.label: Low Pass Filter
options.info: Enables a low pass audio filter to soften the 'harsh' sound of the Pokemon Mini's piezoelectric speaker.

options.label: Low Pass Filter Level (%)
options.info: Specifies the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: Screen Shake Level
options.info: Enable virtual force feedback effect by 'shaking' the screen.

options.label: Controller Rumble Level
options.info: Enable physical force feedback effect via controller rumble.

options.label: Turbo Button Period
options.info: Specify the repeat interval (in frames) when holding down the Turbo A button.

options.label: Internal Palette
options.info: Enables colorization of Supervision games.

options.label: LCD Ghosting
options.info: Simulates LCD ghosting by blending pixels from multiple successive frames. Can help to alleviate the flickering that is common in Supervision games.

options.label: Frameskip
options.info: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.info: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: Fast Memory
options.info: Unstable.

options.label: Force Real Clock Sync
options.info: Slower, less lag.

options.label: Game Language
options.info: 'Automatic' will use the frontend language.

options.label: Rendering Resolution
options.info: Core restart required with Vulkan.

options.label: Buffer Graphics Commands
options.info: GL/Vulkan only, slower, less lag, restart.

options.label: Lower Resolution for Effects
options.info: Reduces artifacts.

options.label: Texture Upscaling Level
options.info: CPU heavy, some scaling may be delayed to avoid stutter.

options.label: Texture Deposterize
options.info: Fixes visual banding glitches in upscaled textures.

options.label: Texture Shader
options.info: Vulkan only, overrides 'Texture Scaling Type'.

options.label: Color Depth (Restart)
options.info: Specifies number of colors to display on-screen. 24-bit may increase performance overheads on some platforms.

options.label: Audio Filter
options.info: Enables a low pass audio filter to soften the 'harsh' sound produced by the Atari 7800's TIA chip.

options.label: Audio Filter Level
options.info: Specifies the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: Dual Stick Controller
options.info: Maps Player 2's joystick to the right analog stick of Player 1's RetroPad. Enables dual stick control in supported games (e.g. Robotron: 2084, T:ME Salvo).

options.label: Cursor > Pointer Device
options.info: Select which device controls the cursor.

options.label: Cursor > Gamepad Cursor Speed
options.info: Sets the mouse cursor speed multiplier when moving the cursor with the RetroPad left analog stick or D-Pad. The default value of '1.0' is optimised for games that have a native resolution of '320x200' or '320x240'. When running 'high definition' games with a resolution of '640x400' or '640x480', a Gamepad Cursor Speed of '2.0' is recommended.

options.label: Cursor > Gamepad Cursor Acceleration
options.info: The amount of time (In seconds) it takes for the cursor to reach full speed

options.label: Cursor > Analog Cursor Response
options.info: Determines how the speed of the cursor varies when tilting the RetroPad left analog stick. 'Linear': Speed is directly proportional to analog stick displacement. This is standard behaviour with which most users will be familiar. 'Quadratic': Speed increases quadratically with analog stick displacement. This allows for greater precision when making small movements without sacrificing maximum speed at full analog range. This mode may require practice for effective use.

options.label: Cursor > Analog Deadzone
options.info: Sets the deadzone in percentage of the RetroPad analog sticks. Used to eliminate cursor drift/unwanted input.

options.label: Cursor > Mouse Speed
options.info: Sets the mouse cursor speed multiplier when moving the cursor with the RetroMouse.

options.label: Cursor > Mouse Fine Control Speed Reduction
options.info: Sets the mouse cursor speed reduction as percentage of normal speed when fine control is activated.

options.label: Timing > Frame rate cap
options.info: Set core frame rate upper limit. Reducing the limit will improve the performance on lower end devices. Changing this setting will reset the core.

options.label: Timing > Sample rate
options.info: Set core sample rate. Reducing the rate will slightly improve the performance on lower end devices. Changing this setting will reset the core.

options.label: Video > Hardware acceleration
options.info: Request video hardware acceleration (OpenGL or OpenGLES2) to the frontend if supported. It is needed to reload the core to apply this setting.

options.label: Video > GUI aspect ratio
options.info: Set ScummVM Launcher aspect ratio.

options.label: Video > GUI resolution
options.info: Set ScummVM Launcher resolution.

options.label: System > Browsing mode
options.info: Select how the ScummVM file browser lists locations. 'Authorized storage' shows the folders authorized through the frontend (e.g. Android SAF trees). 'Local filesystem' browses the standard local paths.

options.label: Console Region (Reload Core)
options.info: Specify which region the system is from. 'PAL' is 50hz, 'NTSC' is 60hz. Games will run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

options.label: Preferred Aspect Ratio
options.info: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

options.label: Crop Overscan
options.info: Remove the borders at the top and bottom of the screen, typically unused by games and hidden by the bezel of a standard-definition television. 'Auto' will attempt to detect and crop the ~8 pixel overscan based on the current content.

options.label: Hi-Res Blending
options.info: Blend adjacent pixels when game switches to hi-res mode (512x448). Required for certain games that use hi-res mode to produce transparency effects (Kirby's Dream Land, Jurassic Park...).

options.label: Blargg NTSC Filter
options.info: Apply a video filter to mimic various NTSC TV signals.

options.label: Audio Interpolation
options.info: Apply an audio filter. 'Gaussian' reproduces the bass-heavy sound of the original hardware. 'Cubic' and 'Sinc' are less accurate, and preserve more of the high range.

options.label: Allow Opposing Directions
options.info: Enabling this will allow pressing / quickly alternating / holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement-based glitches.

options.label: SuperFX Overclocking
options.info: SuperFX coprocessor frequency multiplier. Can improve frame rate or cause timing errors. Values under 100% can improve game performance on slow devices.

options.label: Reduce Slowdown (Hack, Unsafe)
options.info: Overclock SNES CPU. May cause games to crash! Use 'Light' for shorter loading times, 'Compatible' for most games exhibiting slowdown and 'Max' only if absolutely required (Gradius 3, Super R-type...).

options.label: Reduce Flickering (Hack, Unsafe)
options.info: Increases number of sprites that can be drawn simultaneously on screen.

options.label: Randomize Memory (Unsafe)
options.info: Randomizes system RAM upon start-up. Some games such as 'Super Off Road' use system RAM as a random number generator for item placement and AI behavior, to make gameplay more unpredictable.

options.label: Block Invalid VRAM Access
options.info: Some homebrew/ROM hacks require this option to be disabled for correct operation.

options.label: Echo Buffer Hack (Unsafe, only enable for old addmusic hacks)
options.info: Some homebrew/ROM hacks require this option to be enabled for correct operation.

options.label: Show Light Gun Settings
options.info: Enable configuration of Super Scope / Justifier / M.A.C.S. rifle input. NOTE: Quick Menu must be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.label: Light Gun Mode
options.info: Use a mouse-controlled 'Light Gun' or 'Touchscreen' input.

options.label: Super Scope Reverse Trigger Buttons
options.info: Swap the positions of the Super Scope 'Fire' and 'Cursor' buttons.

options.label: Super Scope Crosshair
options.info: Change the crosshair size on screen.

options.label: Super Scope Color
options.info: Change the crosshair color on screen.

options.label: Justifier 1 Crosshair
options.info: Change the crosshair size on screen.

options.label: Justifier 1 Color
options.info: Change the crosshair color on screen.

options.label: Justifier 2 Crosshair
options.info: Change the crosshair size on screen.

options.label: Justifier 2 Color
options.info: Change the crosshair color on screen.

options.label: M.A.C.S. Rifle Crosshair
options.info: Change the crosshair size on screen.

options.label: M.A.C.S. Rifle Color
options.info: Change the crosshair color on screen.

options.label: Show Advanced Audio/Video Settings
options.info: Enable configuration of low-level video layer / GFX effect / audio channel parameters. NOTE: Quick Menu must be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.label: Frameskip
options.info: Skip frames to improve performance.

options.label: Force HLE BIOS (Restart Required)
options.info: Use High Level Emulation BIOS. Not recommended, as it's causing more issues than it solves.

options.label: Add-on Cartridge (Restart Required)
options.info: Emulate an add-on RAM expansion cartridge. Some games require this to be played, while a few others will have improved performance.

options.label: 6Player Adaptor on Port 1
options.info: Enable multitap in port 1.

options.label: 6Player Adaptor on Port 2
options.info: Enable multitap in port 2.

options.label: Number of Threads (Restart Required)
options.info: Depending on your CPU, changing this value can improve performance.
